pr_title: Fix invalid mod combinations potentially being selectable at a game level
pr_body:
- [x] Depends on #11640 (to coexist in the new util class).
- [x] Needs tests.
- Closes https://github.com/ppy/osu/issues/9890.

I also used this in `ModSelectOverlay` (as a replacement for its current logic) but it seems to be pointless. Just PRing in an initial state to make sure this is the intende direction; will add some tests in line with the tests at #11640 in the coming hours/days.
pr_comments: Have manually checked that this does seem to prevent from selecting touch device, but tests would definitely be good to have.

issue_context.title: Touch device mod can get selected on leaderboard scores
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug:** In my investigation, the touch device mod gets selected after other mods are selected (i.e. you can press "use these mods" on a HDTD score and it'll select HD, and then pressing "use these mods" again will add TD to HD). If TD is alone, it'll get selected on first try.

In my attempted PR https://github.com/ppy/osu/pull/9622, we want to disable the context menu entirely if TD is alone, or if not, just prevent TD from being selected at all.

**Screenshots or videos showing encountered issue:** 

![4tskK8Qb7x](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/35318437/90418680-4d85f000-e06a-11ea-8e76-d903e614c0e5.gif)

![PFlC01EHKA](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/35318437/90418743-642c4700-e06a-11ea-8cc0-1ff847624feb.gif)

**osu!lazer version:** 2020.814.0

review_comments: Do we need the `MultiMod` check any more? You are handling the flattening of these in `CheckCompatibleSet` method, which suggests they should maybe be supported as inputs? Or is it never the case that they will be provided for a gameplay scenario?

Actually it technically is kind-of an unsupported input for gameplay purposes... Like if you were to give `Player` a `MultiMod`, neither it nor any ruleset components would know how to deal with it. Whereas on the other hand the `CheckCompatibleSet` method is just checking whether all mods are inter-compatible and assumes the consumer handles `MultiMod`s.

That was my reasoning as to why I left it.
